editorial:
Imagine being a professional at fixing other people's relationships but struggling to plan your own wedding. That is exactly where you find Molly, a former marriage counselor who now runs a hit fitness brand. She is head-over-heels for Nick, a talented wedding photographer who is trying to move into the art world. On the surface, they look like the perfect couple, and the movie gives off a cozy, warm vibe that feels like a big hug. You get to see the stress of wedding planning clash with their personal dreams, making the whole story feel relatable and sweet.

What really works here is the chemistry between the leads, which keeps you rooting for them even when they argue. The pacing is steady, though it follows a pretty standard romance formula, so do not expect any wild shocks. If you want something light to relax with, you should definitely check this out. It is a safe bet for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: After a lot of fighting and a moment where they almost call the whole wedding off, Molly and Nick finally sit down and talk honestly. They realize that their love is more important than a perfect party. They decide to stop stressing over the small details and focus on each other. In the end, they have a beautiful ceremony and officially tie the knot, proving they can handle life's stress as a team.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves lighthearted romance and wedding stories.
